confirmed.firstFrameworkCodesignStderr: error: The specified item could not be found in the keychain.

classification: Actual platform producer failure before fixture generation/native tests. Identity material exists and is usable by importer; default code-sign trust rejected it; the current codesign process did not complete signing.
unproven: The log does not identify which current codesign private API returned the item-not-found message. It does not uniquely prove default trust alone caused that error.
The published Apple open-source tool/framework code is not the exact current macOS codesign binary, and parts explicitly allow untrusted candidates/nonfatal trust failure.

A self-signed leaf may be a legitimate controlled test according to historical Apple macOS documentation, but this does not prove it fixes the current binary under the same no-global-trust constraints.
decision: No speculative certificate-shape, system/user trust-settings/search-list or signing-backend change. Preserve real codesign and exact original CMS verification; add bounded tool execution plus explicit-owned-anchor native policy evidence and verbose current codesign diagnostics.
nextActualSDKDiscriminators: Explicit public owned leaf+root codeSign policy evaluation must run with -r/-L/-N; default-system trust is not established by this result.
If explicit-anchor policy fails, inspect its actual native diagnostic before treating the certificate purpose/constraints as valid.
If local policy passes but codesign still returns item-not-found, the remaining cross-process identity/key access/filtering boundary remains unresolved; do not claim CMS/native execution success.
Only actual codesign exit0 followed by detached primary-CD CMS verification against the explicit owned root can establish the existing producer gate.
stillRequired: A real macOS/Xcode run with the unchanged Keychain/certificate shape and bounded diagnostics, or exact current platform identity-selection evidence. No safe no-global-trust success fix has been established by this Windows/source audit.
